Question: Are French-Canadian and French people the most naturally feminist people in the world?
Answer: The state of feminism in France and Quebec are totally different. I would say Quebec is way more feminist than France. This is subjective, but I feel like Quebec is one of the best places to live in for a woman, but not France. I don’t say Quebec is perfect though. Neither do I say that France is hell on earth. But there are many reasons why I believe France isn’t as feminist as Quebec. One of the main reasons is street harassment. I went to France twice, so I spent maybe 3 weeks there (approximately). In that short amount of time, I was harassed more than I have been my whole life in Quebec. I have been insulted (I think it never happened to me in Quebec), I have been followed in the street, I have been touched, I have been forcefully kissed on the mouth, etc. I would say “no” to some men and they wouldn’t understand at all. It didn’t happen every day, but almost. In Quebec, it happens a few times a year. Recently, Emma, a French cartoonist, visited Montréal. Here are some of the pictures taken from her comic about it. She talks a bit about the differences in the way men and women act together (the translations are under the pictures). There was no street harassement, so it was nice to walk around. (the woman says: It’s even possible to smile!!) I had a lot of interviews and people were very nice. They weren’t rude like in France (they didn’t try to provoke). The man says: “I agree with you when you talk about the mental load, because it’s true that my wife is the one that kept thinking about everything”. She added, in purple: At that moment I asked myself if I couldn’t bring back Québécois to France. → Her comic about the mental load I also once saw a reportage about street harassment in France. They talk about some things I have never ever heard about in Quebec, like “frotteurs” (men who rub themselves against women in the metro). I would like to believe that this is sensationalism, but to be fair, I saw enough street harassment to believe it. That’s sad.

Name: Quelqu'un
Question: What do you think about women who dislike or hate the modern feminist movement?
Answer: I am sad, to be honest. Feminism is the best thing that has ever happened in my life. I have no doubt about that. Feminism is not just about the pop feminism you find on Buzzfeed and other crappy websites. Everytime I hear people complain, they complain about the same type of feminism and the same feminists, but as I said, this is only one type of feminism. Feminism is broad and diverse! There is a feminist community in my hometown and the women are amazing. They are empathetic, smart, open minded, tolerant and strong. As an example, one of them will soon give us a class about how to do basic car repairs. I think it’s such an empowering idea! It helps so many women, even those who chose to believe it’s not good for them. It gives a voice to people who often are not able to talk about their experience. However, I can’t force women who dislike feminism to change their mind. I disagree with them though, I have no doubt about that. But I have female friends who dislike feminism and I still love them nonetheless. I mean… no means no.

Question: Do horror novels have an equivalent of the jump-scare that movies have?
Answer: There is a spoiler from the issue 48 of The Walking Dead in my answer. To be fair, I don’t know how it could be done for a novel. By definition, a jump scare is usually “an abrupt change in image or event, usually co-occurring with a loud, frightening sound” (Wikipedia). So… no, not really. For a comic book I’d say it’s quite possible though. I remember reading The Walking Dead and turning a page, only to see, on the next page, a gruesome picture of Lori being killed by a machine gun while holding her baby (her baby dies too). The whole page was used for that picture. It wasn’t exactly a jump scare, but I was pretty surprised and shocked, so it was kind of the same. Also, the fact I could only see the picture by turning the page made the surprise possible. The picture is here if you want to see it.
